STAR/FOLD · VISUAL REVIEW · 18 OCT 2026

Workspace switching, reconsidered

Ten alternatives to the previous tabs. Compare the workspace controls at actual size, then inspect the complete file manager. Pane styling stays fixed.

Pane treatments ↗

WORKSPACES

Only workspace switching changes. The Refined pane treatment, fonts, and file data stay identical.

Favorites stay in this browser. This HTML works offline.

Comparison rule: the same panes in every option. No repeated close buttons. Several choices have no tab strip at all. Each card shows the controls at 1:1; use “Full layout” to judge the complete application.
Current screenshot · inconsistencies these treatments address
  1. Header hierarchy: FILES and PREVIEW are uppercase, Operations is title case, and the operations count drops to near-microscopic type. Use one header height, case, baseline, and readable count size.
  2. Type roles: filenames, breadcrumb text, controls, status text, and binary text have different apparent sizes and weights. Each option uses an explicit, small type scale with no tiny labels.
  3. Metadata allocation: “MODIFI…”, “58.0 …” and shortened dates appear beside a large unused name column. Reserve complete sizes and dates; let only long names and paths elide.
  4. Tabs: the single tab feels detached from the pane chrome. Compare connected, underlined, numbered, segmented, and softly grouped treatments with the same three workspace names.
  5. Binary preview: the right-edge ellipsis strip has no useful meaning. The preview below keeps complete byte groups and uses eight-byte rows when sixteen no longer fit.
  6. Focus and empty states: a full-height active border competes with selected rows while an empty queue still shows a progress rail. Every option has an explicit focus treatment and a quiet, readable empty queue.
Local workspace-navigation study. The same Refined pane design is used throughout. Workspace switching changes the navigation preview; file contents remain illustrative. HTML is for choosing the native KIT treatment, not an application frontend.
